key_terms.بِالْحُسْنَىٰ: The ultimate goodness, referring to the Hereafter or resurrection

ai.seo_question: What does 'Al-Husna' refer to in the context of Surah Al-Layl?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, 'Al-Husna' (the Best/Hereafter) is often interpreted not merely as the afterlife but as the ultimate station of divine proximity and the Prophet's household (Ahl al-Bayt), whom the disbelievers rejected. This verse underscores the Meccan polytheists' spiritual blindness to the highest form of goodness, linking their denial of resurrection to their rejection of the true spiritual authority. The term thus carries a dual significance of eschatological reward and the supreme status of the Imams.
